title: A Power-Diagram Upper Bound for Twenty-Six Variable-Radius Disks in a Square
summary: Let $S_{26}$ denote the supremum of the sum of the radii of 26 pairwise interior-disjoint closed disks of positive radius contained in the unit square. We prove $2.635983084917607783\ldots \le S_{26}\le \sqrt{\frac{2577}{2500}+\frac{11}{\sqrt3}}=2.716919756099889566\ldots$. The lower bound is accompanied by an exact rational feasibility certificate. For the upper bound, we assign the disks their clipped power cells, convert cell area into a reciprocal exterior-angle cost, and combine this local inequality with Euler side counts.
